newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT-Dlr/mark eyes new highs since 1.7285 break.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Dlr/mark eyes new highs since 1.7285 break.

text.p: The dollar is aiming at new highs after vaulting trendline resistance in the 1.7285 mark area on Monday, technical analysts said.
Resistance was governed by a trendline sloping down from the April 28 high at 1.7389 marks. But with the dollar now trading above 1.73 marks the bullish scenario is reopened.

"Last week was preparation for a break to new highs," said Darren Spain, global foreign exchange analyst at Credit Suisse First Boston. "The downtrend resistance from last Monday's high broke this morning at 1.7285 marks, releasing bullish momentum."
The dollar is expected to make a run for the 1.74 area with initial support now placed at previous resistance by 1.7285, analysts said.
Interim resistance lies at 1.7335 marks, 1.7350 and at last week's cycle high just under 1.74 marks, they said.

"It was a positive move," said Scott Siller, senior technical analyst at MCM CurrencyWatch. "There was bear trendline resistance at 1.73. Also, that was 62 percent of (1.7389 marks) down to (1.7160)."
In dollar/yen the outlook also remains positive, as long as trading is sustained above 126 yen, chartists said.
An 11-day uptrend, off the April 21 low of 125.10, points dollar/yen at 128.40, a new high, Spain said. The chief obstacle to scale remains the May 1 peak at 127.47 yen, a 56-month peak.
At 1120 EDT on Monday, the dollar was trading at 1.7317/22 marks and 126.74/79 yen, up from 1.7285/90 and 126.38/48 at the U.S. open.
